titleStmt.title: Kephalaia of the Teacher, edition page 101: diplomatic and Leiden transcription

sourceDesc.bibl: Kephalaia (Manichäische Handschriften der Staatlichen Museen Berlin), ed. H. J. Polotsky and A. Böhlig, Stuttgart: Kohlhammer, 101. Restorations, sublinear dots, gap counts and corrections are the editors'.

encodingDesc.p: EpiDoc. Read by eye from the page image; gap counts, sublinear dots and supralinear stroke extents verified by measurement on the image. A supralinear stroke is marked on every letter it covers by at least half its width. Spaces are the edition's word division. Facsimile zones are measured line centres. The editors' German statements are not transcribed: each is mapped to an id of the controlled vocabulary data/kephalaia/editorial_vocabulary.json and carried as @ana (ed: statements in the text, app: apparatus footnotes, tr: categories of the transcriber's commentary).

div.p: The manuscript page number ⲣⲁ (top right, odd page) with a bar above and below as the frame (no strokes). Running title > · ⲙⲡⲥⲁϩ · < with its ornaments, no stroke. Every dot run was counted from the dot x-positions. Every ϣ on the page was checked at 6× (one sheet of all fifteen): only 17 ⲛⲁϣϭⲣⲟ has a dot in the lower bowl; all have their tail. Reconcile flags explained: l. 14 the ⲣ dot of ⲛⲣⲱ (1271) lies right of the descender below the window; l. 17 counts the bowl dot of the dotted ϣ (1003) and a piece of "leer" (1213); l. 34 the bracket dots stand at the zone centre (y 1694). Spaces flags are dot runs, enlarged-letter legs (ll. 3, 8, 18, 31) and "leer". Kephalaion 38 (opened 89.18) runs through the whole page; sections open in ekthesis with a restored enlarged letter (ll. 3, 18), after "leer" with an enlarged Ⲡ (l. 8), after "leer" with an ordinary ⲡ (l. 13) and in mid-line with an enlarged Ⲙ (l. 31).
